newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian govt says indicators key to real jobs.
newsitem.headline: Australian govt says indicators key to real jobs.

text.p: Australian Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone said on Friday the government needed to get all indicators right before creating lasting jobs.

"We are trying what we believe is the most responsible way to resolve unemployment - and that is to get all the indicators right for business to create real lasting jobs," Vanstone told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.

"We wouldn't have got into government after 13 years of opposition and gone into such a tight fiscal strategy ... if we didn't believe it was in the best interest of the country and in particular the best way to generate real jobs," Vanstone said.
On Thursday the Australian Bureau of Statistics said its national employment estimate fell 40,300 in May, prompting economists to say the economy was weaker than previously thought.
"I understand there is still some apprehension about whether the economy is on the right track," Vanstone said.

"And the reason for that, is people have gone through 13 years of boom and bust under Labor and they see low interest rates now and they're still a little bit apprehensive about whether that is going to continue because they've been used to a very cyclical arrangement in the economy," she said.
"And they're not sure yet that we're into what we want to be into -- which is a period of long term stable growth and stable interest rates," she said.
Prime Minister John Howard said late on Thursday that the pickup in the Australian economy was now evident.
He said investment figures and lower interest rates would feed into the labour market next year, creating a much stronger employment figure.
Gross domestic product grew 0.9 percent in the March quarter to a level 2.4 percent higher than a year before.
Howard also said recent rate cuts were yet to be fully felt.

The Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy in July, November, December and May, each time dropping its overnight cash rate target by 0.5 percentage points. It now targets overnight cash at 5.5 percent.
